verdict: Prologis collected more rent as leases reset higher — revenue rose 8% to $2.4B and GAAP profit was $880M, helped by $108M of gains from selling properties.

segments.name: Rental
segments.note: Rent and tenant recoveries from logistics warehouses around the world — the core business, up 7% as leases signed earlier at higher rents kicked in.

segments.name: Strategic capital
segments.note: Fees for managing warehouse funds owned with partners, plus promotes — asset-management income on top of the rent.

segments.name: Development management and other
segments.note: Development management fees and other revenue — small, and up sharply from $9M a year ago.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back-office and management costs of running the platform — $128M.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of warehouse buildings over their long lives — a non-cash charge, and the main reason GAAP profit is far below FFO for a landlord.

otherDetail: Gains on property sales added $108M ($52M from development properties and land, $56M from other real estate) and earnings from unconsolidated ventures added $155M, against $287M of interest expense, partly offset by $65M of currency, derivative and other gains — $41M net. The bottom line here is consolidated GAAP net earnings of $880M; $816M of it was attributable to common stockholders after noncontrolling interests and preferred dividends.

takeaways.title: Rent is still resetting higher
takeaways.text: Rental revenue rose 7% to $2.2B. On the same-store portfolio, Prologis' share of cash NOI rose 5.9% — leases signed at higher rents are flowing into the numbers.

takeaways.title: Core FFO rose 7% a share
takeaways.text: Core FFO — the landlord metric that adds back building depreciation — was $1.60 per share, up from $1.49. Full-year guidance is $6.25–$6.29 of Core FFO per share.

takeaways.title: Depreciation is the GAAP gap
takeaways.text: Depreciation and amortization of $710M is a non-cash charge for wearing out buildings that are, in market terms, generally holding or gaining value — which is why FFO ($1.5B) dwarfs GAAP profit.

oneTimers: Gains on dispositions added $108M before tax: $52M from selling development properties and land and $56M from other real estate sales. These are a recurring part of Prologis' build-and-sell model, but they are not rent.
footerNote: Prologis is a REIT: this flow is GAAP, with consolidated net earnings as the bottom line. Core FFO ($1.60 per share) is a non-GAAP landlord metric shown only as a KPI chip.
